title: 2024 AHA/ACC Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Acute Coronary Syndromes
content: Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) encompasses ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), and unstable angina. Immediate initial pharmacological therapy includes dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with high-dose aspirin (162-325 mg initial loading dose) and a P2Y12 inhibitor (ticagrelor 180 mg or prasugrel 60 mg). Sublingual nitroglycerin (0.4 mg) should be administered every 5 minutes for up to 3 doses for ongoing ischemic chest pain, provided there is

content: for ongoing ischemic chest pain, provided there is no right ventricular infarction or recent phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor use. High-intensity statin therapy (atorvastatin 80 mg or rosuvastatin 40 mg) must be initiated early regardless of baseline LDL cholesterol level. Invasive coronary angiography within 24 hours is strongly recommended for high-risk NSTEMI patients displaying elevated cardiac troponin, recurrent angina, or dynamic ST-segment changes.

NICE Guideline NG106: Chronic Heart Failure in Adults: Diagnosis and Management
content: For patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, LVEF <= 40%), foundational quad-therapy should be introduced promptly: (1) an ACE inhibitor or Angiotensin Receptor-Neprilysin Inhibitor (ARNI such as sacubitril/valsartan), (2) an evidence-based beta-blocker (bisoprolol, carvedilol, or nebivolol), (3) a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (spironolactone or eplerenone), and (4) a sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor (dapagliflozin or empagliflozin). Loop diuretics (e.g., furosemide 20-40 mg daily) are indicated for symptomatic relief of congestion and fluid overload.

title: IDSA/ATS Consensus Guidelines on the Management of Community-Acquired Pneumonia in Adults
content: Outpatient empiric antimicrobial therapy for adult community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) without comorbidities or MRSA/Pseudomonas risk factors consists of amoxicillin (1 g three times daily) or doxycycline (100 mg twice daily). Macrolides (azithromycin 500 mg day 1, then 250 mg daily) are recommended only in areas with pneumococcal macrolide resistance < 25%. Inpatient non-severe CAP requires a beta-lactam (ceftriaxone 1-2 g daily) plus a macrolide (azithromycin 500 mg daily) or a respiratory fluoroquinolone.

Efficacy of SGLT2 Inhibitors in Diabetic Kidney Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
content: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors significantly reduce renal disease progression, cardiovascular mortality, and heart failure hospitalizations in patients with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease (CKD). Analysis of 12 randomized clinical trials (n = 48,210) demonstrated a 37% relative risk reduction in the composite renal outcome (sustained eGFR decline, end-stage kidney disease, or renal death; HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.56-0.72). content: The initial transient decline in eGFR ('eGFR dip' up to 30%) observed within 4 weeks of starting SGLT2 inhibitor therapy is hemodynamically driven by reduction in intraglomerular pressure and should not trigger premature drug cessation unless associated with acute clinical volume depletion.
